> A round of operator-found fixes across nearly every verb, plus a root-host init fallback, scoped credential-bridge wiring, and wrong-copy app-update detection.

### Upgrade Steps

* [ACTION REQUIRED] Update cwcli to v3.2.0.
* [ACTION REQUIRED] On a shared-mode machine that uses the credential bridge, you can now scope it to specific instances with `cwcli config cred-bridge enable --project <name>` instead of it wiring every running Frappe container.
* [ACTION REQUIRED] If a site was left in maintenance mode by an earlier `migrate` or `apps update` that was killed or lost its terminal, `cwcli status <project>` now names it directly; run the command it prints (`cwcli run <project> --site <site> set-maintenance-mode off`) to clear it.

### Breaking Changes

* `cwcli rm <project-that-does-not-exist>` now exits 1 with a plain not-found warning, matching `rm-site`/`rm-bench`; it previously printed the destructive-deletion banner alongside the error and still exited 0.
* `cwcli config cred-bridge enable` now wires only cwcli-managed instances by default, and refuses (rather than silently skipping) an explicitly named `--project` that is not cwcli-managed.
* The human `cwcli status` web line now prints the reachable host address instead of the container-internal port.
* A broken pipe (for example `cwcli ... | head`) now exits quietly by signal instead of returning exit 1.

### New Features

* `cwcli init --uid <n>` overrides the uid cwcli aligns the container's `frappe` user to, and `init` on a root (uid 0) host no longer fails: it now keeps the image's default frappe uid instead of aliasing the container's own root account, and warns once.
* `cwcli list` and `cwcli instances` now work as aliases for `ls` (and `apps ls` for `apps list`); a bare `cwcli status` with no project prints the all-instances summary instead of a usage error.
* `cwcli doctor` gains a check that flags a dev/editable install running behind its tracked upstream branch.
* `cwcli config cred-bridge enable --project <name>` (repeatable) scopes the credential bridge to named instances; an unscoped sweep touching more than one instance now announces its targets before wiring.
* `cwcli status` reports when a site is stuck in maintenance mode and names the command to clear it.
* `inspect` and `apps list` flag an app whose `apps/<app>` is a symlink or whose imported copy differs from what's on disk, and `apps update`/`apps checkout` no longer report success when they changed a copy the running site doesn't actually use.

### Bug Fixes

* A killed terminal or a plain `kill` during `migrate`, `apps update`, `apps checkout`, `apps install`, `run-tests`, or `restore` no longer leaves a site stuck in maintenance mode or leaks credential-bridge leftovers (socket, shim, git config line) - SIGTERM and SIGHUP now unwind like Ctrl+C.
* A failed `apps install` no longer poisons every later retry with a half-fetched app directory; the partial directory is now cleaned up, and a present-but-invalid one gets an actionable message instead of a traceback.
* `cwcli rm`'s pre-backup database readiness probe no longer false-fails a healthy, slow-to-start instance, and a real failure now names the specific cause (connection refused, unresolvable host, exec failure) instead of a bare timeout.
* `cwcli init` validates the project name before the admin-password check, so an invalid name is reported on the first attempt.
* `backup`, `unlock`, `restore --latest`, and `axi migrate` now fall back to a bench's sole site instead of failing with "no default site found"; a multi-site bench lists the available sites in the error.
* `apps install` accepts the app name positionally, matching `apps update`/`apps checkout`.
* A failed `apps update` pull now shows a tail of git's real error by default.
* A supervisor-install failure during `start`/`restart` now shows the actual captured output instead of always blaming a network connection.

### Other Changes

* `bench init` no longer runs with a hardcoded `--verbose`, and the Docker Hub bench-tag lookup is now cached and skipped when an image tag is pinned, making a plain `cwcli init` noticeably faster and quieter.
* Several wording fixes: "not found" messages are consistent across verbs; a stopped instance's cached benches are reported as "not running" instead of "0 benches"; `init --reuse-bench` says "Reused bench" instead of "Successfully initialized bench"; the human `rm-bench` running-bench refusal names the real bench selector.
